# Results — Study 827 (Cross-Asset Skewness Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
asset-class analogue of the single-name realized-skewness reversal (Amaya, Christoffersen,
Jacobs & Vasquez 2015; cf. Study 803): sort the major asset classes on their **trailing
realized return skewness** and go long the low-skew / short the high-skew book; low-skew
classes should out-earn. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Fingerprint `9ce7d7c0e243` (nine-ETF Close panel).*

*Sample pinned as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `9ce7d7c0e243`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **nine asset-class ETFs**, 2007-01-03 → 2026-06-30, **4,903** dated rows |
| Universe | a fixed nine-ETF cross-section of the major asset classes — SPY (US equity), EFA (dev-ex-US), EEM (EM), TLT (long Treasuries), LQD (IG credit), HYG (HY credit), GLD (gold), DBC (commodities), VNQ (REITs); cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each class's **trailing-126-day realized skewness** of daily simple returns (population third standardised moment, vectorised via `m3 / m2**1.5`), sampled at each **month-end** |
| Sort | each month rank the nine classes by the signal known at the **prior** month-end; **long the bottom ⅓** (low skew, 3 classes), **short the top ⅓** (high skew, 3 classes), equal-weight; hold the following month |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal at month-end `m−1` → hold month `m`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per monthly rebalance on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 6-lag) *t* on the monthly spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled low-vs-high books; a 1,000-permutation asset-label placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `TICKERS` is a **current-membership** set of the
nine canonical, liquid class-proxy ETFs. Because it is small, fixed and low-turnover (the flagship
class ETFs have not been delisted over the sample), the survivorship exposure is **far milder** than
a single-name universe — but the caveat still travels with every published number.

## The headline — long-low-skew / short-high-skew spread

Monthly equal-weight bottom-⅓ minus top-⅓ realized-skew spread across the nine classes
(n = **227** months, median 9 classes ranked/month):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long low-skew − short high-skew)** | **+13.73 bps/month** |
| Newey-West(6) *t* | **+0.62** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.64 |
| low-skew book / high-skew book | +63.24 bps / +49.51 bps (Welch *t* = +0.39) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost, annualised) | +0.15 |

The spread's **sign is in the claimed direction** — the low-skew classes did edge out the
high-skew ones — but the magnitude is **statistically indistinguishable from zero** (NW *t* =
+0.62). At the asset-class level there are only nine names and a handful of skew "regimes," so the
single-name lottery-overpricing effect has almost nothing to bite on. The claimed premium is
**absent**, not merely small.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) spread a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing-skew sort but read each month's forward returns from an **asset-label-permuted**
panel (signal → outcome link broken, each month's cross-sectional return distribution preserved),
1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+13.73 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.42 bps (17.10) |
| position of observed | ≈ **0.83σ into the right tail** (right-tail p = **0.204**) |

The observed spread sits barely four-fifths of a standard deviation above a null centred at zero —
one in five permuted worlds beats it. There is **no evidence** the sort captured anything real.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2016-07-01) and the window sweep

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2007-08 → 2016-07 (n=107) | **−15.21 bps** | −0.45 |
| 2016-07 → 2026-06 (n=120) | **+39.54 bps** | +1.39 |

| trailing skew window | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 63 days | +22.06 bps | +1.04 |
| **126 days (headline)** | **+13.73 bps** | **+0.62** |
| 252 days | +5.95 bps | +0.25 |

The spread **flips sign across the two halves** (negative early, positive late) and never clears
*t* = 2 at any lookback. This is a series with no stable sign, not a robust premium.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per monthly rebalance on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/mo | cost/mo | net/mo | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +13.73 bps | 6.17 bps | **+7.57 bps** | +0.35 | +0.08 | +0.9%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +13.73 bps | 14.17 bps | **−0.43 bps** | −0.02 | −0.00 | −0.1%/yr |

Even the gross spread is insignificant; after a token 5 bps one-way it is exactly zero. There is no
paycheck to collect. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded closes panel (nine synthetic assets) with a persistent latent "skew tilt" that
shapes each asset's return skewness and (with `edge>0`) depresses its forward mean. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.01** (sd 1.22), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.004`, seed 827) | **+2.52** (Welch *t* = +2.87) |

The detector recovers a *planted* low-skew/high-return relation cleanly (it clears the significance
bar even on a nine-asset cross-section) and stays ~silent on the null — so the flat real-tape result
is a genuine **absence of edge**, not a broken sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The single-name realized-skewness reversal does **not** carry up to the
  asset-class level. The long-low-skew / short-high-skew spread across nine class ETFs is
  **+13.73 bps/month** (NW *t* = **+0.62**) — right-signed but statistically zero, sitting only
  ≈0.83σ into the right tail of a 1,000-permutation placebo (p = 0.20), flipping sign across the two
  eras (−15.21 / +39.54 bps), and insignificant at every lookback (63/126/252-day *t* =
  +1.04 / +0.62 / +0.25). The synthetic control shows a real premium of plausible size *would* have
  fired, so this is an honest null, not a machinery failure. With only nine classes there is too
  little cross-sectional skew dispersion for the effect to exist.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross spread is already insignificant (Sharpe +0.15); a mere 5 bps
  one-way cost erases it to zero (+7.57 bps/mo net at 1 bp, *t* = +0.35). Nothing survives friction
  because there was nothing there to begin with.
